video_title: Jalen Duren Feels 'Disrespected' By $200M Offer By Pistons

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren's contract negotiation and dissatisfaction with the Detroit Pistons
quotes.excerpt: He feels disrespected, he doesn't feel wanted in Detroit.
quotes.quote: The reporting is that he has been offered five years, $200 million with weight clauses in the contract that are built as bonuses for him, and he is not taking it. He feels disrespected, he doesn't feel wanted in Detroit. But boy, $200 million on the table for you for over five years and you are like, no thanks, I feel disrespected. I feel disrespected after I just pooped the bed in the playoffs and they are giving me $200 million. What disrespect? Let's be serious. It is not disrespectful. The Pistons are negotiating against themselves right now offering $200 million. Get the hell out of here.

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Speculation on Jalen Duren potentially joining the Sacramento Kings
quotes.excerpt: I think he has got a team, and I think that team is in all likelihood the Sacramento Kings.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
text_blocks.text: I think he has got a team, and I think that team is in all likelihood the Sacramento Kings. The team that has been all along, that the Kings are already in and willing to pay Jalen Duren any amount as long as the Detroit Pistons are willing to sign him to that deal and sign and trade him to the Kings for what it is that they would get back.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
text_blocks.text: Earlier in the off-season when there was the rumor of Jalen Duren for Domantas Sabonis, I was like, no, if I were Detroit, no. Sabonis can't defend. He is a low-volume shooter. But Tom, you are still there. But at this point, do you really want to bring back Jalen Duren, unhappy, doesn't want to be there, potentially taking the qualifying offer, could walk for nothing in the year, and a year you can't trade him if he takes the qualifying offer? It puts you in a position where you could be wasting this year.

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Critique of Domantas Sabonis's defensive and offensive impact
quotes.excerpt: I have never been a big believer in Sabonis, I think he is a zero on the defensive end.
quotes.quote: I am not the biggest Sabonis fan, Kings fans know this. I have never been a big believer in Sabonis, I think he is a zero on the defensive end. Offensively, I think he creates some issues for you with the lack of consistent spacing, low-volume shooter, and I am just not a Sabonis guy. But Detroit is interesting because of pairing Sabonis with Ausar Thompson and some of their other tough wing defenders, maybe Sabonis can be good enough positionally and offer elite rebounding on defense, that it doesn't matter that you downgrade from Duren to Sabonis on defense when Sabonis is so much more dynamic on the offensive end of the floor.

quotes.speaker: Tom Haberstroh
quotes.summary_phrase: Analysis of Jalen Duren's post-season performance and weight concerns
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Duren had an all-time collapse in the post-season.
quotes.quote: I think the weight clause thing is fascinating to me. Jalen Duren had an all-time collapse in the post-season. We are talking about a guy who was 22 years old and all-NBA. And normally in this league, that means max the hell out of that guy. If you are a 22-year-old rising to be a top-15 player in the season with a 60-win season under your belt, that screams max that guy. Look at what he did last year. He was awesome when Cade Cunningham was out. He was awesome when Ausar Thompson was out.

quotes.speaker: Tom Haberstroh
quotes.summary_phrase: The personal nature of weight and body criticism in contract negotiations
quotes.excerpt: Anytime you are having a disagreement with someone and then they point at your weight, your body.
quotes.quote: Anytime you are having a disagreement with someone and then they point at your weight, your body and says, hey, this is an issue that I am having is the way you look, the way your body is. I could see Jalen Duren being like, yeah, I just with this body that you are trying to put weight clauses in this contract, I was third team all-NBA. I was all-star at age 22 and I was anchoring the defense with Ausar Thompson for a 60-win team a lot of the times that that Cade Cunningham who famously was not eligible for the post-season until he pressed the double secret probation button and he was able to get that exemption.

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin O'Connor's past skepticism regarding Jalen Duren's consistency
quotes.excerpt: I am done with Jalen Duren. He is too inconsistent, he can't be trusted.
quotes.quote: I remember I had Bryce Simon, who covers the Pistons, on my podcast in the middle of the 24-25 season. And I said to Bryce, I am out. I am done with Jalen Duren. He is too inconsistent, he can't be trusted. He is hot, he is cold. He looks like a dominant defender one night and then he is just a terrible paper mache interior guy the next night. That was the 24-25 season and then he got better the end of that year. And then the 25-26 season, he is an all-NBA guy.

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Jalen Duren to former Celtic Mark Blount
quotes.excerpt: The Celtics player I hated the most, Mark Blunt. Obviously Jalen Duren is much better than Mark Blunt.
quotes.quote: I remember in my childhood, the Celtics player I hated the most, Mark Blunt. Mark Blunt. Obviously Jalen Duren is much better than Mark Blunt ever was. But Mark Blunt in his contract year was great. He was so good in his contract season with the Boston Celtics and they signed him to like a four-year $28 million deal or something along those lines. Big money at the time. And then he went from really good to horrific again. Just up and down, inconsistent, couldn't trust him, so annoying and overpaid.

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Why the Pistons are including weight clauses in Duren's contract
quotes.excerpt: I think that is why the Pistons are building in the weight clauses.
quotes.quote: I think that is why the Pistons are building in the weight clauses. I think that is why the Pistons are unwilling to offer the full max, because it is not just how much he sucked in the playoffs, it is about how inconsistent he has been over the first four years of his career. That is what I think it is, both combined on top of the roster concerns that you are talking about. That said, he is 22 years old. He just had a year where he was an all-NBA player. He did show real progress in a lot of different ways.
